## Exercises  {#Exercises_DataReshaping}

### Exercise 2 {-}

Using the `datasets::trees` data, complete the following. This question refreshes create a linear model, graphing the linear model, and introduces using some LaTeX expressions on the graph.

**a)** Create a regression model for $y=$ `Volume` as a function of $x=$ `Height`.

```{r}
?trees
model <- lm(Volume ~ Height, data = trees)
data <- trees %>% mutate(fit = fitted(model))
```


**b)** Display the `summary` of the  model to view the y-intercept and slope of the regression line.

```{r}
summary(model)
```


**c)** Using `ggplot2`, create a scatter plot of Volume vs Height. 

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + geom_point()
```


**d)** Color the scatter using the `Girth` variable.

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + geom_point(aes(color = Girth))
```


**e)** Modify the color scheme using a RColorBrewer palette.

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + geom_point(aes(color = Girth)) + scale_color_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1)
```


**f)** Create a nice white filled rectangle to add text information. The following might be useful.

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + geom_point(aes(color = Girth)) + scale_color_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1) +
annotate('rect', xmin=65, xmax=75, ymin=60, ymax=74, 
         fill='white', color='black') 
```

**g)** Use the `broom` package to extract the coefficients of the best-fit line. Add this information as an annotation to the graph, which should follow a form that looks like $\hat{y}_i = (INTERCEPT) + (SLOPE)* x_i$. Place the annotation within the white text box.

```{r}
tidy <- broom::tidy(model)
#tidy
intercept <- round(tidy$estimate[1], 2) 
#intercept
slope <- round(tidy$estimate[2], 2) 
#slope
eq <- str_c("$\\hat{y}_i = ", intercept, " + ", slope, " * x_i$")

ggplot(data, aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + geom_point(aes(color = Girth)) + scale_color_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1) + annotate('rect', xmin = 65, xmax = 75, ymin = 60, ymax = 74, fill = 'white', color = 'black') + annotate('text', x = 70, y = 70, label = TeX(eq), size = 3.5)
```


**h)** Use the `broom` package to extract the coefficient of determination $r^2$ from the model. Add the annotation to your graph, which should look something like $R^2 = (VALUE)$

```{r}
glance <- broom::glance(model)
r_sq <- round(glance$r.squared, 3)
r2_eq <- str_c("$R^2 = ", r_sq, "$")

ggplot(data, aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + geom_point(aes(color = Girth)) + scale_color_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1) + annotate('rect', xmin = 65, xmax = 75, ymin = 60, ymax = 74, fill = 'white', color = 'black') + annotate('text', x = 70, y = 70, label = TeX(eq), size = 3.5) + annotate('text', x = 70, y = 64, label = TeX(r2_eq), size = 3.5)
```


**i)** Add the regression line in red. There are several ways to do this.

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + geom_point(aes(color = Girth)) + scale_color_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1) + geom_line(aes(y = fit), color = "red") + annotate('rect', xmin = 65, xmax = 75, ymin = 60, ymax = 74, fill = 'white', color = 'black') + annotate('text', x = 70, y = 70, label = TeX(eq), size = 3.5) + annotate('text', x = 70, y = 64, label = TeX(r2_eq), size = 3.5)
```

**j)** Properly label the axes of the graph.

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + geom_point(aes(color = Girth)) + scale_color_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1) + geom_line(aes(y = fit), color = "red") + annotate('rect', xmin = 65, xmax = 75, ymin = 60, ymax = 74, fill = 'white', color = 'black') + annotate('text', x = 70, y = 70, label = TeX(eq), size = 3.5) + annotate('text', x = 70, y = 64, label = TeX(r2_eq), size = 3.5) + labs(x = "Height (ft)", y = "Volume (cubic ft)", color = "Girth (in)")
```


**k)** Add a descriptive title to the graph.

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + geom_point(aes(color = Girth)) + scale_color_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1) + geom_line(aes(y = fit), color = "red") + annotate('rect', xmin = 65, xmax = 75, ymin = 60, ymax = 74, fill = 'white', color = 'black') + annotate('text', x = 70, y = 70, label = TeX(eq), size = 3.5) + annotate('text', x = 70, y = 64, label = TeX(r2_eq), size = 3.5) + labs(title = "Black Cherry Tree Timber Volume vs. Height", x = "Height (ft)", y = "Volume (cubic ft)", color = "Girth (in)")
```
